notes: Method: Airbnb blocks WebFetch but not curl with a browser user-agent, so I ran ~55 dated map-bounded Airbnb searches for checkin=2026-12-19 / checkout=2026-12-27, adults=9, min_bedrooms=5, max_bedrooms=6, parsed the embedded data-deferred-state JSON, and then fetched 79 individual listing pages with the same dates to pull room-by-room bed configuration, stated guest capacity and amenity lists. Every price below is a real Airbnb 8-night quote for the actual trip dates (total before taxes), not an estimate. That produced 185 unique 5-6BR listings, 171 of them on the mainland after filtering out the Gulf barrier islands (Clearwater Beach, Sand Key, Indian Rocks, Madeira, Treasure Island, St Pete Beach). Twelve further zoomed searches on Davis Islands, Old Northeast, Snell Isle, Shore Acres, Tierra Verde, Hyde Park/Bayshore, Safety Harbor, Dunedin, Tarpon Springs, Seminole Heights, Temple Terrace and Oldsmar added exactly one new listing, so coverage is saturated. Blocked: Vrbo and HiChee search pages both refuse curl (429 / 301-Cloudflare); individual Vrbo listing pages fetch but carry far thinner structured data than Airbnb, and the Vrbo candidates I chased in Tierra Verde turned out to be 2-4 bedroom homes. What the right-sized market actually looks like here: the 5-6BR / sleeps 9-12 band is real but thin, and it is dominated by two clusters. Cluster one is north Pinellas — Palm Harbor, Dunedin, Safety Harbor, Tarpon Springs, Lake Tarpon — where you find genuine five-bed/five-bedroom houses with docks, fireplaces and heated pools at $3,600-$8,000 for the eight nights. Cluster two is inner Tampa (Ybor Heights, North Hyde Park, Seminole Heights, Tampa Heights) where the houses are older, more characterful and walkable but rarely have pools. The prestige waterfront neighbourhoods the family might imagine — Davis Islands, Snell Isle, Old Northeast, Bayshore, Tierra Verde — are almost empty at this size: those streets are owner-occupied, and the handful that do rent are either 3-4BR or priced at $20k+ for the week. The dominant failure mode in this region is the west-Clearwater 'sleeps 18-20' party villa (mini golf, bowling lane, 11-16 beds crammed into 5-6 bedrooms) — there are dozens of them between Largo and Clearwater and I have deliberately excluded all of them. Three kings is genuinely scarce: of 171 in-region listings, only about eight have exactly three kings with a sensible capacity. Heated pools are rarer still and worth confirming directly with the host, since Airbnb's amenity data only states 'heated' for a minority of listings.

properties.name: 6 min Downtown in Ybor Heights — 5BR / 5BA Two-Story
properties.beds_note: Bedroom 1 queen; Bedroom 2 king; Bedroom 3 king; Bedroom 4 queen; Bedroom 5 king. Five bedrooms, five beds, no bunks, no sofa beds.
properties.price_note: Airbnb quote returned in a dated Dec 19-27 2026 search for 9 adults: $4,243 total for 8 nights before taxes (~$530/night).
properties.why: The cleanest match in the whole region: exactly three kings for the three couples and two queens for the three twenty-somethings, five beds for five bedrooms, and five full bathrooms so nobody queues. Capacity is capped at 10, so it is priced and laid out for a group this size rather than for a bunk-room crowd, and it is six minutes from downtown Tampa and walking distance to Ybor's Seventh Avenue.
properties.cons: No pool, which is the one thing a December Florida week really wants. Ybor Heights is a transitional neighbourhood — fine, but not the polished Hyde Park streetscape. 4.8 rating is good rather than outstanding.

properties.beds_note: Bedroom 1 king; Bedroom 2 double; Bedroom 3 king + sofa bed; Bedroom 4 king; Bedroom 5 queen.
properties.price_note: Airbnb quote returned in a dated Dec 19-27 2026 search for 9 adults: $8,740 total for 8 nights before taxes (~$1,092/night).

properties.why: Three kings, a queen and a capacity of 10 on open water — an infinity saltwater pool and heated spa looking straight out over Tampa Bay, a private dock you can fish from, manatees and dolphins off the seawall, and an indoor fireplace for the cool evenings. This is the one that feels like a proper Christmas-week waterfront house rather than a rental.
